articles.title: Gentle, a new financial intelligence platform, launches in India: Reading the market through the portfolio you actually own
articles.summary: Gentle, a new financial intelligence platform, rolled out its mobile app today.
articles.body: Gentle, a new financial intelligence platform, rolled out its mobile app today. The platform aims to help the next generation of Indian investors make better sense of their portfolios by linking market developments to their actual holdings and explaining their potential implications in simple, accessible language. India's retail investor base has grown rapidly over the past few years, but the tools available to track and understand their growing portfolios have not kept pace. Investors often rely on separate apps for equities, mutual funds and portfolio tracking while financial news remains generic and disconnected from what they hold. Gentle was built to close that gap, combining a unified portfolio view with a curated news feed and plain-language explainers that surface only the updates relevant to a user's own investments.“Most young Indians I know are doing well and still can’t answer one simple question: Is my money okay? It’s currently scattered across five apps, an Excel sheet and a CA’s PDF. We built Gentle to bring it into one place and explain, in plain English, what the market means for what you own” said Vishvesh Patel, Founder of Gentle.Gentle launches with three core features.Portfolio brings a user’s entire investment picture into a single view, covering stocks, mutual funds, REITs, InvITs and ETFs, along with harder-to-track assets such as AIFs and unlisted shares.News delivers a personalised feed shaped by what users hold, what they follow and how they use the app. Each story explains its impact on the economy, the sector and where relevant, the user’s own holdings, while a general market feed alongside it offers the bigger picture.Discover lets users explore listed companies, mutual funds, IPOs and more, each paired with plain-language context on what the business does and what drives it.Gentle Money is now available on iOS and Android.Disclaimer - The above content is non-editorial, and TIL hereby disclaims any and all warranties, expressed or implied, relating to it, and does not guarantee, vouch for or necessarily endorse any of the content.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Sensex slides 1,484 points as global market weakness weighs on D-Street investors
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Global AI-led market sell-off got the better of Dalal Street's month-long foreign funds-led rally on Monday with the sensex closing 1,484-point
articles.body: MUMBAI: Global AI-led market sell-off got the better of Dalal Street's month-long foreign funds-led rally on Monday with the sensex closing 1,484-point down at 82,436 points. Profit taking by local traders after nearly a 15% gain in the last one month also helped the slide in the indices, market players said.Selling was concentrated in banking and financial services, metal and select energy stocks while Indian IT stocks, which are now being considered safe havens from the global AI-led sell-off, saw some smart up moves, they said. The day's session also left investors poorer by a little over Rs 5 lakh crore with the combined market capitalisation of companies listed on the BSE now at Rs 509 lakh crore, exchange data showed. On NSE, nifty lost 451 points or 1.8% to close at 25,350 points. During Monday's session, sensex opened higher but soon entered the negative territory and eventually slid over 2,200 points from the day's high as selling picked up pace.Of the 30 sensex stocks, 22 closed in the red. Among these, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Axis bank contributed the most to the index's loss in the day.On BSE, bankex, the banking sector index lost 3.1% while on NSE, nifty bank index closed 3.2% down.According to Vinod Nair, head of research, Geojit Investments, last week's late global sell-off, triggered by concerns over an AI bubble and tighter US monetary policy, weighed on Indian equities on Monday. On Friday night in the US, Nasdaq Composite index had crashed 5.3% while S& slid 3.7% and Dow Jones index was down 2%."Global cues remained fragile, with Asian markets tracking Friday's sharp sell-off in the US technology stocks. Concerns over elevated AI valuations, the sustainability of AI-led capital expenditure and the unwinding of crowded technology positions continued to erode risk appetite, spilling over into domestic equities and reinforcing a cautious trading environment," added Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, a wealth-tech platform. Indian markets are closed on Tuesday for Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev, BSE said on its website.The day's 1.8% slide in sensex came despite a Rs 5,673-crore net buying by foreign funds. So far this month, foreign portfolio investors have net pumped in nearly Rs 1.4 lakh crore into Indian equities, combined data from NSDL and BSE showed. During Monday's session, domestic funds were net sellers with the net outflow at Rs 2,760 crore, BSE data showed.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: IDBI not govt bank: SC; staff interest protected: Centre
articles.summary: New Delhi: The Supreme Court has held that IDBI is not a \"State\" within Article 12 of Constitution, which means it was not a govt entity, dealing a blow
articles.body: New Delhi: The Supreme Court has held that IDBI is not a "State" within Article 12 of Constitution, which means it was not a govt entity, dealing a blow to the the bank's officer's association, even as govt maintained that the interests of employees and pensioners of the bank have been fully protected.Last week, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran dismissed an appeal filed against a 2022 decision of the Bombay High Court, which struck down demand of the association, that called for retirement and provident fund benefits for employees of United Western Bank, which had merged with IDBI, arguing that the Centre retained administrative, functional and financial control over IDBI till 2018 and LIC, which acquired stake in the bank, was also owned and controlled by govt.The SC ruling will also have an implication on the "strategic restructuring" of IDBI Bank, where govt and LIC are selling over 60% stake held by in the bank to Fairfax. Employees have called for scrapping the sale, questioning the valuation and arguing that benchmarking it to public sector stock was not proper as IDBI is a private bank. Govt has also allayed concerns over retirement and salary benefits.When contacted, DIPAM secretary Arunish Chawla said: "Govt and LIC are not employers under the Labour Code. IDBI Bank is the employer under the Code. A strategic transaction is executed through a share purchase agreement within the framework of the Contract Law. DIPAM appoints transaction and legal advisers, who in turn consult with the qualified parties on the one hand and with the bank management on the other. IDBI is a board-run banking company and management consults the employees internally, and has in this case presented a very robust protection framework for employees and pensioners, which is the best ever granted in such transactions. The service conditions of existing employees cannot be changed, modified or altered to their disadvantage after the strategic restructuring. The IDBI management has made sure all the service rules framed by the board are included in the annexures to the draft agreement. The pensioners are also fully protected, there is a special fund for it and their pension benefits will be full honoured."Asked about the controversy over valuation of two properties, Chawla said Cuffe Parade headquarters in Mumbai was on 60-year lease and valuation was based on the rental saving for the remaining 25 years of lease. In the case of the training centre in Hyderabad, the property cannot be transferred in the open market and comparing its value to market-auctioned property would have been "absurd".Money habits form by age 7.
